title: MarshalGateRecord
description: The dict shape core.egress.build_gate_record() produces (Story 2.6, AD-34): a durable record of one completed gate evaluation -- the commands run, their exit codes, the scope-check verdict, the tree revision, and a UTC ISO-8601 timestamp. additionalProperties is false at both the document and the commandReport level, matching policy.json's/envelope.v1.json's own closed-schema discipline. This schema describes the dict shape build_gate_record() RETURNS, before core.egress.to_redacted() is applied. For a record built by build_gate_record(), redaction only ever replaces string CONTENT with the sentinel -- it never adds, removes or retypes a field -- so a redacted gate record still validates against this same schema, and a test asserts exactly that. The general to_redacted() serializer has one shape this claim does NOT cover (review finding, verified live): two DISTINCT token-shaped mapping KEYS both rewrite to the sentinel and therefore collapse into one entry, dropping a field. build_gate_record's field names are fixed and none is token-shaped, so no gate record can reach that case. jsonschema validates this document only in tests (src/ never runtime-validates against it, matching policy.json's own precedent).

story.description: The canonicalized story key (AD-23/AD-38), e.g. "2.6" or "6.1a" -- core.identity.normalize()'s one dot form. Named "story", not "story_key": the latter ends in the _KEY suffix core.policy.is_secret_key matches, which would redact the record's own story identifier on every real to_redacted() call.

commands.description: One entry per configured verify command, mirroring core.gate.classify_outcome's own report shape.

scope_check_verdict.description: The scope-check verdict (Story 2.3, not shipped yet), or null -- the only value any real caller can supply today.

tree_revision.description: An already-gathered fact identifying the evaluated tree state -- this schema does not prescribe its format (e.g. a git SHA). The \S pattern rejects a whitespace-only value that minLength alone admits (review finding, verified live), matching build_gate_record's own .strip() check: a record identifying the evaluated tree as "   " proves nothing.

timestamp.description: A UTC ISO-8601 timestamp (zero tz offset), parsed -- never generated -- by build_gate_record(). The pattern is kept character-for-character identical to core.egress._TIMESTAMP_PATTERN and a test pins the two spellings together, so the SPELLING half is enforced identically on both sides: a bare 'type: string' let the schema green-light records (a hand-written one, or one from a non-Python consumer) that build_gate_record rejects outright, e.g. "yesterday afternoon" or a +05:00 offset, and datetime.fromisoformat's greater permissiveness let the producer emit four legitimate UTC forms this pattern rejects -- a missing seconds field, the compact offsets +0000/+00, and the basic form 20260803T000000Z. Every date/time component also carries its real range (review finding, verified live): with bare [0-9]{2} groups this pattern accepted 2026-13-45T99:99:99Z, and 2026-08-03T24:00:00Z passed BOTH sides while fromisoformat silently resolves hour 24 to the NEXT day -- a durable record whose stored text and meaning disagree. One asymmetry REMAINS and is stated rather than claimed away: a regex cannot express calendar validity, so 2026-02-30T12:00:00Z matches this pattern while build_gate_record rejects it via fromisoformat. A consumer needing that guarantee must parse the value, not only validate it.

commandReport.description: One verify command's already-classified report. The allOf below ENFORCES the two invariants the property descriptions state in prose (review finding, verified live: without it a self-contradictory entry -- resolvable false AND returncode 0 AND captured stdout -- validated clean against this contract, which core.egress.build_gate_record itself rejects). For a record whose purpose is proving months later what was checked, an internally false entry is worse than a rejected one; a non-Python consumer reads this schema, not the Python validator.

command.description: The verify command string, as configured. The \S pattern rejects a whitespace-only value that minLength alone admits (review finding), matching build_gate_record's own .strip() check.

returncode.description: The process exit code, or null when the command never ran (resolvable: false).

resolvable.description: Whether the command actually ran to completion (classify_outcome's own field).

stdout.description: Captured stdout -- present only when resolvable is true.

stderr.description: Captured stderr -- present only when resolvable is true.
